Post-demerger, Vedanta declares first interim dividend of ₹5 per share
items.summary:
Vedanta Ltd on Thursday declared an interim dividend of Rs 5 per share for the current financial year, amounting to about Rs 1,955 crore.
This is the company's first interim dividend post-demerger, reinforcing the company's focus on delivering value to shareholders as it enters a new phase as a more focused and diversified natural resources company, the company stated in an exchange filing.
"... the board of directors of Vedanta Limited have, today, i.e. October 08, 2026, approved the first interim dividend 2026-27 of Rs 5 per equity share on face value of Rs 1 per equity share for the financial year 2026-27 amounting to Rs 1,955 crore," Vedanta said in the filing.
The dividend comes soon after a strong Q2 FY27 operational performance, with Vedanta reporting broad-based momentum across its businesses. The company recorded record quarterly and half-yearly production across key operations, with particularly strong performance in zinc, ferro alloys, ports and aluminium.

items.summary:
Vedanta Ltd on Thursday declared an interim dividend of Rs 5 per share for the current financial year, amounting to about Rs 1,955 crore.
This is the company's first interim dividend post-demerger, reinforcing the company's focus on delivering value to shareholders as it enters a new phase as a more focused and diversified natural resources company, the company stated in an exchange filing.
"... the board of directors of Vedanta Limited have, today, i.e. October 08, 2026, approved the first interim dividend 2026-27 of Rs 5 per equity share on face value of Rs 1 per equity share for the financial year 2026-27 amounting to Rs 1,955 crore," Vedanta said in the filing.
The dividend comes soon after a strong Q2 FY27 operational performance, with Vedanta reporting broad-based momentum across its businesses. The company recorded record quarterly and half-yearly production across key operations, with particularly strong performance in zinc, ferro alloys, ports and aluminium.

items.summary: Indian equity markets showed signs of recovery on Monday after softer-than-expected US jobs data was released. The Nifty 50 index ended the session up, suggesting improved investor confidence. Investors are watching key corporate updates from companies like Vedanta and Kotak Mahindra Bank for future trends. This fixed-dose inhaler combines three therapies into a single device for better treatment outcomes. It aims to benefit over 55 million people living with COPD across the country. The Drug Controller General of India has approved this innovative product for use. Lupin is currently ranked second in the respiratory therapy segment in India.
